# Add an element

**The finished shape:** `src/main/java/com/playwrightplayground/tests/pages/networkmocking/` (the page, its elements and actions) and `src/test/java/com/playwrightplayground/tests/cases/NetworkMockingFormTest.java`, the suite's worked example (README.md, "Write a test"). What follows is only what to add.

The crawl's own are already there: every button, field and dropdown it saw with a locator it
trusts is in the page's Elements, above the YOURS block, with a method that uses it
(`enter().email(...)`, `click().send()`, a `fill...Form(...)` task). Add one here only for what the
crawl did not see (it appears after a click, behind a login, after a form is sent), or for a fragile
one controls/<Page>.md lists and says why.

Before adding one, **search the Elements for its locator**: an element already there under another name
(a story before you added `SIGN_IN_BUTTON`; you would add `LOGIN_BUTTON`) is used by that name. The
suite's rules fail one element under two names (SR-22).

Elements live in the page's Elements enum (`HomeElements` for HomePage), in its **elements** YOURS block:

```java
    // ==== YOURS (elements): safe to edit; regenerating keeps what is between these lines ====
    SIGN_UP_BUTTON(page -> page.locator("xpath=//form[@id='newsletter']//button[@type='submit']")),
    EMAIL_INPUT(page -> page.locator("css=#newsletter input[type='email']")),
    // ==== END YOURS (elements) ====
```

- **Name** it SCREAMING_SNAKE, ending in what it is (`_BUTTON`, `_INPUT`, `_LINK`, `_HEADING`,
  `_TEXT`, ...). Steps call it by that: "Click the sign up button". If that reads badly, give the
  constant a label: `SEND_BUTTON(...) { @Override public String label() { return "the Send button"; } },`
- **Look it up first** in controls/<PageClass>.md (controls/HomePage.md for HomePage) and controls/Everywhere.md:
  each button, field and dropdown the crawl saw, by the words a story would use, with a line to paste
  here. Its locator matched exactly one element when the crawl read the page. Rename the constant if
  the story calls it something else.
- **Or find it in the page as crawled**: crawl/pages/<path>.html, then check what you write finds exactly
  one element: `suite locate playwright-playground-com-tests <page> "<locator>"` where Suite Builder is installed.
- **Otherwise take the locator from a saved page** (use-a-saved-page.md), never guess. Prefer, in order: a
  test id (`data-testid`, `data-test`), an id that is not generated (no digits soup), a name or
  label, the visible text, a short path from a stable parent. Avoid positions (`[3]`) and class
  names with hashes (`css-1x2y3z`).
- **With the site open in Chrome**: Selector Grabber, a free extension (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/gjpelpkcfkikaflgljfgfipblpcmocei),
  gives a locator for any element you point at, in that same order; the crawl used the same engine for the controls it saw (controls/, when it saw any).
- **A heading** (h1-h6, a table header, a label): `CONTACT_US_HEADING(page -> Headings.named(page, "Contact Us")),`.
  It matches the heading's whole text; Playwright's `text="..."` misses a heading written as
  `Contact <strong>Us</strong>`.
- **Repeated elements** (one per row): add a locator method with a parameter in the **extras**
  block, like the generated `get...Link(name)` methods.
- If the same element also sits hidden somewhere (a mobile menu), add `>> visible=true` and
  `.first()` as the generated ones do.
- The element is on every page (a search box in the header): it goes in HeaderElements instead.
